I work on **integral field spectroscopy** — observations that record a full
spectrum at every point in an image rather than a single spectrum for a whole
object. That turns a picture of a nebula into tens of thousands of spectra, and
the interesting problem becomes extracting a physical quantity from all of them
at once without losing track of the uncertainty.

My current data comes from the [Local Volume
Mapper](https://www.sdss.org/dr19/lvm/) (LVM), one of the three surveys in
SDSS-V. I am focused on the 30 Doradus region of the Large Magellanic Cloud.
